description:
The HUD velocity readout on /fly shows 'NaN km/s' for the entire cruise to any outer-planet destination (Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, Pluto, Ceres).

Expected: The HUD displays a finite heliocentric speed (km/s) at every point on any trajectory. The NaN originates in heliocentricSpeed() in fly-physics.ts where the vis-viva radicand 2/r − 1/a goes negative because a is hardcoded to 1.262 AU (Earth-Mars Hohmann) — when the spacecraft's heliocentric distance r exceeds 2 × 1.262 ≈ 2.524 AU, Math.sqrt produces NaN and no guard catches it.

Acceptance criteria:
- heliocentricSpeed(rAu, aTransferAu) must return a finite number for every finite positive rAu and aTransferAu — including when 2/rAu < 1/aTransferAu (negative radicand) and when rAu ≤ 0. [code-invariant: NaN is never a valid speed display; Math.sqrt of a negative number is always a bug.]
- Existing passing tests in fly-physics.test.ts must continue to pass: Earth-circular (29.78 km/s), Mars-circular (24.13 km/s), Hohmann perihelion (32.73 km/s). [code-invariant: fly-physics.test.ts lines 24-33 — regression would break established contract.]
- Moon mission HUD values must not regress — the isMoonMission path in +page.svelte that uses R_EARTH_AU as both r and a must not be touched. [spec: +page.svelte lines 942-948 comment: 'For HUD honesty we use Earth's heliocentric radius for vis-viva so HELIO ΔV reads ~29.78 km/s consistently (the spacecraft co-orbits with Earth during transit).']

Domain facts:
- Earth semi-major axis ≈ 1.000 AU (R_EARTH_AU)
- Mars semi-major axis ≈ 1.524 AU (R_MARS_AU)
- (R_EARTH_AU + R_MARS_AU) / 2 ≈ 1.262 AU → 2a ≈ 2.524 AU is the outer-planet NaN threshold
- Jupiter a=5.203 AU, Saturn a=9.537 AU — all far exceed 2.524 AU
- DESTINATIONS[activeDestination].a is available at the call site already imported (DESTINATIONS imported at +page.svelte:65)

Target: src/lib/orbital/fly-physics.ts — heliocentricSpeed
Do NOT change src/routes/fly/+page.svelte — it is not the owner of this symptom.
